parameters.content:
## Vera 05 · 09 Send on WhatsApp
The only way Vera sends anything. Picks session message or template by the 24-hour window, logs every message id (so replies bind to lines), backs off on rate limits, and never fails silently.

Generated from `n8n/mobilise/workflows.mjs`. Edit there and rebuild; edits made here are overwritten on the next import.
Each node's note says what it does and which guardrails it carries.

nodes.name: Asked to send
nodes.notes: Who, what, and why (kind / area / line).

nodes.name: Load contact and window

parameters.query: select $1::bigint as contact_id, c.phone, c.last_inbound_at, c.role from contacts c where c.id = $1;

nodes.notes:
Phone and when they last wrote to us.
Guardrails: retry

nodes.name: Session or template?
nodes.notes:
Inside 24 h of their last message: the message itself (free). Outside: the approved template, or not sent.
Guardrails: window

nodes.name: Can send?
nodes.notes:
No phone, or outside the window with no template: not sent, logged.
Guardrails: window

nodes.name: Log not sent

parameters.query: insert into outbound (mobilisation_id, contact_id, kind, area, line_code, ref, payload, status, error) values ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7::jsonb, 'not_sent', $8::jsonb) returning id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [($('Asked to send').item.json.mobilisation_id) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.contact_id) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.kind) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.area) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.line_code) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.ref) ?? null, (JSON.stringify($('Asked to send').item.json.request)) ?? null, (JSON.stringify({ why: $json.why || $json.send_error && $json.send_error.note })) ?? null] }}

nodes.notes:
Shows up in the daily ops list.
Guardrails: human, audit

nodes.name: Send to WhatsApp
nodes.notes:
Graph API messages endpoint.
Guardrails: error-out, timeout

nodes.name: Log what we sent

parameters.query: insert into outbound (wamid, mobilisation_id, contact_id, kind, area, line_code, ref, payload) values ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8::jsonb) returning id, wamid;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [($json.messages[0].id) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.mobilisation_id) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.contact_id) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.kind) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.area) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.line_code) ?? null, ($('Asked to send').item.json.ref) ?? null, (JSON.stringify($('Session or template?').item.json.payload)) ?? null] }}

nodes.notes:
The message id is what makes "reply to this message" bind for sure.
Guardrails: audit, retry

nodes.name: Why did it fail?
nodes.notes: Reads the WhatsApp error code: rate limit, window closed, bad number.

nodes.name: Retry?
nodes.notes: Rate limit → wait and retry (max 3). Window closed → template. Bad number → a person.

nodes.name: Wait 30 s
nodes.notes: WhatsApp limits how fast one person can be messaged.
